sourceNotes.text: The earlier account links a day/month inscription, renovation context and fragility to an autumn date. The reported date has no year; other words have competing readings.
On 17 October 2023, oak charcoal was applied to ancient plaster on the same wall, at about 180 cm.
Temporary roofing excluded rain; intermittent sunlight, wind and rising damp remained. Three brief coverings were reported.
Photographs used a color reference; twelve dates are listed. Figure 4 includes 24 August 2024; figure 5 ends at 17 August.
Authors report continued legibility, with pressure-dependent differences and slight fading.
Separate removal trials tested dry/wet methods and simulated rain; deliberate removal differs from passive survival.
Environmental comparability and interrupted renovation are author interpretations. Conclusions allow an earlier inscription year without establishing the eruption day.

premiseExercise.kind: Original editorial counterfactual; neither measured data nor a dating engine.
fixedAssumptions: For this exercise only, accept the reported day/month reading.
For this exercise only, assume the reported date refers to creating the mark, rather than a past event it mentions. This is an added premise, not established by reading a date.
Assume the mark precedes the destruction being considered and remains in its original context.
Any independent-year toggle is hypothetical; this dossier does not establish that year.

inputs.meaning: Independent evidence fixes the mark’s year, rather than deriving it from freshness.
Relevant differences between modern and ancient conditions have been addressed sufficiently for the stated comparison.
The selected modern observation is accepted for the exercise; switching off is withholding assessment, not evidence that it failed.

outputs.conditional-lower-bound-only: With the fixed assumptions, the destruction cannot predate the reported calendar day in the independently anchored year; it could occur later that day or on a later day. No exact eruption day follows.
outputs.year-unresolved: A month/day and an unanchored year do not produce a dated calendar lower bound.
outputs.analogy-challenges-short-survival-exclus: The analogous result challenges using inevitable early disappearance to exclude an older mark. It supplies neither a universal lifetime nor a probability.
outputs.local-modern-result-only: The modern result remains evidence for its tested setting; transfer to ancient conditions has not been justified.
outputs.modern-result-not-assessed: This exercise adds no preservation inference; it does not establish the opposite by default.

unsupportedOutputs: An asserted measured effect size from rendered image darkness
premiseExercise.presentation: Three clearly hypothetical premise controls with a persistent observed-source table. Every control and output needs an ordered text equivalent; changing an assumption must not rewrite the evidence.

activities.prompt: Separate what is reported as visible, what is interpreted and what needs an additional premise. Identify the source span for each.
activities.assessment: Do not let an inferred value move into the observation column without new evidence.

activities.prompt: Build a method checklist: specimen, setting, intervention, observation schedule, outcome and transfer limits. Keep each entry attached to its locator.
activities.assessment: Do not mix different intervention arms or treat an author’s comparability argument as a controlled demonstration.

activities.prompt: Compare the full series, the paired comparison and the prose. Explain which source locator answers each timing question.
activities.assessment: A selected pair is not automatically the full observation schedule; no missing or conflicting observation is inferred solely from the pair.

activities.prompt: Use the eight original counterfactual cases. Explain which conclusion changes when one premise changes, and name evidence needed to justify that premise.
activities.assessment: Possibility, lower bound, typical behavior and exact event date are different conclusions. A counterexample to inevitability does not estimate prevalence.

activities.prompt: Separate an announcement, an accessible research body, supplements and a completed independent methodological check. State what each permits you to conclude.
activities.assessment: A later title or institutional announcement is a discovery lead, not proof that an earlier argument has been superseded.
